reviews.text: Very professional service, they are very attentive!
I had my kitten's first appointment at this clinic and I highly recommend it! They are professional, attentive, and the premises are clean and modern.

Absolutely INCREDIBLE!!!
My little Blast had to be looked after by the Entrechat team and kept under observation!
It was incredibly well-organized and stress-free, and communication was excellent!
The vet sent me photos of the kitten every evening with a little note, and I was even able to visit him! Anyway, all I can say is thank you for such a lovely space, both in terms of decor and the staff. I don't know what else to say! You can go there with complete confidence!!

PS: Blast thanks you too 🧡💛🤎🐾

2021: A very good experience. A kind, attentive team who seemed to genuinely love animals. They were very good with my cat, who is usually very fearful but not at all aggressive.

2023: After an illness requiring an ultrasound, Ness's behavior changed with the vets, becoming more aggressive than he had ever been with anyone. We never really found out what had happened to him.

2026: The problems started again. An ultrasound showed signs that could suggest cancer, but the subsequent blood test was presented to us as rather reassuring. We were told about a possible low- or medium-grade lymphoma, with a biopsy needed to confirm. Despite a 25% weight loss and the fact that he wasn't gaining weight, we were advised to keep him at home since he was still eating. At our request, the file was finally transferred to Mermoz Vet, where we quickly obtained an appointment for the least invasive biopsy, which unfortunately proved unusable.

Ness sadly passed away shortly afterward. The diagnosis mentioned elsewhere was that of a very aggressive high-grade lymphoma.

It was primarily this progression that profoundly shattered our confidence: from a lymphoma initially presented as potentially low/medium grade, then more reassuring following the blood test results, we moved to a very aggressive high-grade lymphoma, even though Ness had already lost 25% of her weight.
Lovely vets, clean and pleasant premises. They gave excellent advice. They supported us and our two pets through thick and thin.
A very welcoming, kind, and attentive team! We rescued a small stray animal and received excellent support and advice.

I highly recommend your services.

I absolutely do not recommend this veterinary clinic. My experience was very negative, and personally, I will not be returning or taking my animals there again. I advise doing thorough research and comparing with other veterinarians before going.

Regarding the positive reviews, after my experience, I find them very difficult to understand, and I don't know to what extent they truly reflect reality.

Our two cats, Petrus and Tilly, have been seen by Dr. Oger for several years. Thank you for your feedback! :D

A true nightmare.

I entrusted my 3-year-old cat to the dentist for a dental cleaning. For about a month, he had red gums and tartar buildup, but he was eating normally, hadn't lost weight, and his overall health was good. A five-day course of anti-inflammatory medication had even led to a significant improvement in his symptoms.

Before the procedure, we were told that two of his back teeth might need to be extracted. It was based solely on this information that we gave our consent.

To our utter astonishment, after the "cleaning," we discovered that 17 teeth had been removed, including both upper canines, without us having been consulted before such a drastic decision. The justification given was that the left canine was heavily coated with tartar. So why was the second canine also removed, along with 14 others that weren't planned? We never gave our consent for such a procedure.

At no point were dental X-rays offered or shown to us to explain or justify these extractions. Or medication for a conservative approach. No second opinion or consultation with a veterinary dentist was offered, even though this was a decision with irreversible consequences.

I'm now getting back a cat whose face has changed and who will have to learn to eat differently. The loss of his two long upper canines alters his expression and will remind me of this procedure every day.

The hardest thing to accept is that no other solution was considered or, at the very least, discussed with us. Faced with the extraction of 17 teeth, the minimum required is further examinations, clear explanations, and, if necessary, a referral to a veterinarian with dental expertise. None of this was offered to us.

Today, I can't help but wonder if this major procedure was truly the only option. I will request the complete medical file for review. I have the distinct impression that the decision to extract 17 teeth was made with disconcerting ease, without the owners having any say in the matter.

This experience has shattered the trust I had placed in this clinic. Had I been informed that an extraction of this magnitude, including the two upper canines, was a possibility, I would have immediately sought a second opinion from a specialist veterinarian and had this major procedure performed by qualified surgeons.

I will now live with the regret of not having done so, as well as with the irreversible functional and morphological consequences of this decision for my cat.

Edit: Confirming the diagnostic hypotheses (PCR for the virus in question, pre-operative X-ray) before such a major procedure, plus a follow-up post-operative X-ray after extraction, seems to me to be the bare minimum. Surgery is a specialty I would have sought out for my pet's well-being. And I would, at the very least, have a follow-up X-ray done, as required by any guidelines. We did not misunderstand - you did not inform us of your viral hypotheses and it was a question of the extraction of 4-5 teeth not 17.
Exceptional welcome! A true love of cats! Very good care.

I have been taking my cat to this clinic for several years. This year, she required more care following a liver infection, which was diagnosed and treated with great kindness by the clinic's veterinarians.

I had a terrible experience with this veterinary clinic following my cat's surgery. I had been taking my cat's annual checkups to this clinic for three years, and everything was fine, except that I had to see a different vet each year. However, at the end of 2025, my cat had to have surgery for a lump on his lower abdomen. The surgery itself went well, but the post-operative care was disastrous… no Elizabethan collar was offered, the dressing was very basic… and as a result, the wound became infected! I had to make several visits to the clinic, and once again, I saw a different veterinarian each time who wasn't necessarily familiar with the follow-up care…
But the worst lack of professionalism, in my opinion, was that after having a drain inserted in my cat, I had an appointment for Saturday, October 29, 2025, at 8:00 a.m. to have it removed, and then on Friday, October 28, 2025, the evening before, at 7:48 p.m., the clinic manager sent me an email saying "there was no need to come to the appointment the next day"!!! What the clinic manager couldn't accept was my discussions with her staff, my legitimate dissatisfaction, and the fact that I could question their post-operative care… I was met with a complete lack of self-reflection on their part.

Despite this, I accept the disagreement we may have had, but what I find intolerable is leaving an animal in distress with its drain and then canceling an appointment the day before. I believe it would have been far more professional to keep the appointment, ensure the animal's safety, and then inform me that the "client relationship" was ending. For me, this is unacceptable and unworthy of professionals who are supposed to respect animal welfare.

I don't usually leave negative reviews, and in fact, I had decided against it, but given their numerous reminders for my cat's annual check-up (automated messages), even though they were the ones who removed me from their clientele, I have definitively concluded that this clinic demonstrates a lack of professionalism, which I felt compelled to report.
Great! You can entrust them with your furry monsters without a second thought!

My little Moon goes there regularly for his checkups, and I'm always delighted with the welcome and professionalism of the entire team. You can tell they genuinely love animals and take care of our little cats with so much gentleness and attention.
Moon is always pampered with love, which is very reassuring as an owner.
Even on the phone, the team is available, caring, and always ready to answer questions. It's a real pleasure to trust them!

I don't understand this clinic; it seems like there are two rooms, two completely different atmospheres, judging by the positive reviews!
For my wife's cat, they missed an obvious diagnosis: old cat + unspayed + discharge that wasn't urine = pyometra.
We were sent elsewhere for an ultrasound because the only vet who knew how to perform them wasn't there—and this was at a clinic with several vets. Our cat was mistreated: I heard him howling upstairs when they removed a bandage… and they claimed our cat was aggressive. He was my wife's cat, and I've rarely seen such a gentle and easy-to-handle animal. You can see it in the second photo: it was his first visit there, and this supposedly aggressive cat was sleeping peacefully. After an operation, they left our old cat lying in his own urine… Honestly, if it had been up to me, I would have taken legal action against them. We were far too busy trying to clean up the mess our cat had been in anyway.

To clarify: I was the owner of this cat, who died from gastrointestinal lymphoma that the clinic couldn't diagnose—in addition to pyometra, which they also failed to detect. We had to change vets to finally get a diagnosis, unfortunately too late. Our new vet was able to make it in ten minutes with a simple ultrasound. This happened two years ago.

After the total hysterectomy, I got my cat back in a terrible state: lethargic, terrified, and covered in her own urine. I was able to see her "behind the scenes," and my friend, who was with me, was also shocked by her condition and the way she was being treated. The cat had lain down in her urine-soaked litter box—no absorbent pad, and no one had thought to change the litter. I was told she was aggressive, which was the only clinic to confirm: none of the other vets who saw her had ever had this problem. I was able to move her without any equipment despite her pain—and a vet isn't supposed to be afraid of a cat, especially when they have the proper equipment. So I decided to take her straight home without waiting until evening, even though they wanted to insert a feeding tube because she wasn't eating. I refused, following my instinct, and she eventually started eating on her own again at home—even though it would have required another anesthetic for the tube insertion, on a cat I was already half-dead when I got her home. It's not right to return an animal in that state.

After the hysterectomy, another veterinarian at the clinic greeted us with a "your cat is aggressive" as soon as we arrived, without even examining her—and didn't retract his statement when he realized that wasn't the case. The last visits she had with other veterinarians before her death went very well, even though she had become more fearful because of that bad experience.

In short, we changed veterinarians, and since then, with my other cats, we haven't had a single misdiagnosis and none of my animals have been afraid of vet visits.
Thank you to this clinic and its veterinarians for existing. You can feel their love for our little kitties and their great professionalism. I highly recommend it to all cat parents ❤️
Thank you for your feedback :)

Zara, Nikita, Logan, Piou Piou, Moïse, Mercedes, Miller, Marley, and Fifille

This review is not written in the heat of the moment, but after careful consideration and consultation with several veterinary professionals. I believe it is my responsibility to warn other pet owners.

In short: if you are looking for a competent veterinarian who respects animal welfare and is capable of handling situations calmly and with experience, I do not recommend this clinic.

I consulted for my cat after she suddenly developed a limp in her left front leg. She was calm but no longer put weight on her paw.
The veterinarian who saw us, Dr. Tess Eiselé, performed the examination with the help of a colleague. That's when things went downhill.

1️⃣ Very poor restraint
Instead of using appropriate techniques, they tried to restrain her with an unsterilized blanket and a pair of extremely thick, dirty gloves, visibly covered in dried blood stains. Their restraint method completely failed: my cat struggled, the pain worsened, the joint visibly twisted further, and she began to tremble alarmingly.

2️⃣ Hasty Use of Anesthesia
The veterinarian insisted: “I won’t touch her unless she’s anesthetized.” Yet, it was only a palpation.
In other, more experienced clinics, examinations are performed without the routine use of anesthesia, especially in cats, which are particularly sensitive to anesthetics.

3️⃣ Incomplete Radiographic Examination
Only one X-ray (lateral view) was taken, despite persistent inflammation and a visible change in the paw’s posture. No frontal view, no examination of the lymph nodes, and no attention paid to the wound found on her elbow.

😥After this consultation, my trust was deeply shaken.

I consulted other veterinarians who all confirmed that these practices are neither standard nor acceptable.

➡️ This experience has left a mark on me, and I wouldn't wish this kind of treatment on any animal.
A good veterinarian knows how to restrain an animal without traumatizing it.
A responsible veterinarian doesn't prioritize their own safety over the animal's health.

Anesthesia should never become a means of comfort for the caregiver.

I'm leaving this review so that others can make an informed choice.

😾7/4/2026: I also wish to respond to the clinic's reply.

I regret that the heart of the matter is being avoided by focusing on my animal's supposed condition rather than the actual conditions of the procedure during the consultation.

I would like to clarify some observable facts:

– the initial restraint was not properly applied (unsecured limb positioning, incomplete wrapping),
– the use of equipment that was clearly unsuitable and did not meet rigorous hygiene standards,
– an immediate worsening of my animal's reaction (struggle, trembling, increased pain).

Following this incident, several veterinarians I consulted expressed reservations about these practices, particularly regarding the management of the restraint and the rapid use of anesthesia.

I want to clarify that I am not opposed to anesthesia in itself. However, I believe it should not become an easy solution when appropriate and controlled restraint would allow for a basic clinical examination.

My intention is not to gratuitously attack anyone, but to report a specific and verifiable experience, while respecting the right of other pet owners to information. (For clarification, the identity of the practitioner mentioned was verified using publicly available information (name and photograph) on the clinic's official website.)
